s1.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae, starting at birth, with a waxing and waning course, and involving the face, trunk, and extremities
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
Vesicles and bullae on the face, trunk, and extremities
key_facts: Born to healthy, nonconsanguineous parents
Normal growth and development for age and sex
Unremarkable family medical history
Initial exam showed multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae
Vital signs were within normal ranges
Mucous membranes not affected
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis
Direct immunofluorescence results were unremarkable
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1
Later developed thickened, brown, corrugated plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae, starting at birth

shortlist.label: Pemphigus Foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis

shortlist.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Waxing and waning course with involvement of face, trunk, and extremities

shortlist.label: Erythema Multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on the face, trunk, and extremities

shortlist.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, with genetic testing revealing a heterozygous variation in KRT1

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratosis, distinct vacuolization in the granular and upper spinous layers, and bullae formation within the epidermis, along with the genetic testing revealing a heterozygous variation in KRT1, supports the diagnosis of Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Pemphigus Foliaceus
rejected.why: Unremarkable direct immunofluorescence results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
rejected.why: No linear IgA deposits were mentioned in the direct immunofluorescence results

rejected.label: Erythema Multiforme
rejected.why: The presence of hyperkeratosis and bullae formation, along with the genetic variation in KRT1, is more consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic testing results do not support this diagnosis
